products.overview: Manual sample preparation doesn't scale, and it doesn't stay reproducible either. Labomatic's Liquid Handling platform is built to remove both problems at once. At its core is the LABOMAT LH-5000, a modular X/Y/Z liquid handling platform for analytical and preparative applications, available in over 1000 size and configuration variations through its building-block design. Combinable modules add fraction collection, autosampling, aliquoting, pooling, cleaning, and data storage, all freely programmable and controllable through a touchscreen or Labomatic's own LaboChrom 5 software.
features: Modular Building-Block Design: X and Y elements combine into over 1000 different size and configuration variations.
Extensive Multi-Axis Travel: Up to 2800mm on the X-axis, 800mm on the Y-axis, and 500mm on the Z-axis.
Parallel Multi-Axis Processing: 2 Y-axes, each supporting up to 2 Z-axes, for genuine simultaneous operation.
Freely Programmable Control: Operate via onboard touchscreen or directly through LaboChrom 5 software.
Combinable Application Modules: Fraction collection, data storage, cleaning, autosampling, aliquoting, and pooling modules work together on one platform.
Customer-Adapted Axis Height: X/Y axis height configured to match your specific application requirements.
Solvent-Resistant Construction: Built to withstand aggressive solvents in demanding lab environments.
Optional RFID Identification: Supports sample or vessel tracking where traceability matters.

faqs.question: What is Labomatic's Liquid Handling platform used for?
faqs.answer: The Labomatic Liquid Handling platform, built around the LH-5000, automates sample preparation, fraction collection, and related liquid handling tasks for analytical and preparative applications. It's designed to eliminate manual sample handling and improve reproducibility.

faqs.question: How many configurations does the LH-5000 come in?
faqs.answer: The LH-5000's modular building-block design allows more than 1000 different size and configuration variations, adapting the platform to a customer's specific dimensions, sample count, and sample volume.

faqs.question: What is the travel range of the LH-5000?
faqs.answer: The LH-5000 offers X-axis travel from 160mm to 2800mm, Y-axis travel from 70mm to 800mm, and Z-axis travel up to 500mm, depending on configuration.

faqs.question: Can the LH-5000 run multiple applications at once?
faqs.answer: Yes, the largest LH-5000 configurations support up to 5 simultaneous applications, using up to 4 Z-axes and 2 Y-axes for parallel processing.

faqs.question: What modules can be added to the LH-5000?
faqs.answer: Available modules include LABOCOL fraction collection, data storage, and cleaning modules, along with LABOPORT autosampler, aliquot removal, and pooling modules, all combinable on the same platform.

faqs.question: How is the LH-5000 controlled?
faqs.answer: The system is freely programmable and can be controlled through an onboard touchscreen or directly through Labomatic's LaboChrom 5 software.

faqs.question: Is the LH-5000 resistant to aggressive solvents?
faqs.answer: Yes, the platform's construction is built to withstand aggressive solvents commonly used in laboratory purification and handling workflows.

faqs.question: Does the LH-5000 support sample tracking?
faqs.answer: Yes, an optional RFID identification system is available for sample or vessel tracking.

faqs.question: What is the price of Labomatic's Liquid Handling platform in India?
faqs.answer: Pricing depends on the specific axis configuration, size, and modules selected for your application. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed with Labomatic.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of Labomatic's Liquid Handling platform in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for Labomatic Liquid Handling systems in India. Inkarp provides demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

body: The platform is built to eliminate tedious manual sample preparation while increasing reproducibility and system uptime.
Its base unit, the LH-5000, uses a building-block system of X and Y elements that combine into more than 1000 different size and configuration variations.
Effective travel reaches up to 2800mm on the X-axis, up to 800mm on the Y-axis, and up to 500mm on the Z-axis, with axis height adaptable to the customer's specific application.
The largest platform configurations reach up to 3000mm in width and 1200mm in depth, supporting up to 4 Z-axes and 2 Y-axes, with up to 5 applications running simultaneously.
It's a multi-axis system, with 2 Y-axes each capable of carrying up to 2 Z-axes, adding real parallel-processing capability rather than a single fixed arm.
The system is freely programmable, controlled either through an onboard touchscreen or directly through Labomatic's LaboChrom 5 software.

Combinable application modules extend the base platform for fraction collection, data storage, cleaning, autosampling, aliquot removal, and pooling, and different applications can be combined on the same system.
Construction is built to withstand aggressive solvents, and an RFID identification system is available as an option for sample or vessel tracking.

sections.title: The LH-5000 Modular Platform
body: Most liquid handling platforms come in a handful of fixed sizes. The LH-5000 takes a different approach, building the entire base unit out of combinable X and Y elements.

That building-block construction is what gets the platform to over 1000 different size and configuration variations, with practically no limitation on dimensions, sample number, or sample volume. Effective travel reaches up to 2800mm on the X-axis, 800mm on the Y-axis, and 500mm on the Z-axis, and axis height itself can be adapted to fit the customer's specific application. On the largest configurations, that scales up to 3000mm in width and 1200mm in depth, with up to 4 Z-axes and 2 Y-axes supporting as many as 5 applications running at the same time.

sections.title: Application Modules Explained
body: The base LH-5000 platform is the movement system. The modules are what turn that movement into an actual workflow, and they're designed to be combined rather than chosen one at a time.

The LABOCOL fraction collector module automates collection directly off the platform, while the LABOCOL data storage module keeps run data logged and accessible. A LABOCOL cleaning module supports consistent cleanup between runs. On the LABOPORT side, the autosampler module automates sample introduction, the aliquot removal module handles precise sub-sampling, and the pooling module combines fractions or samples as your method requires. Because the platform is freely programmable and modules are combinable, several of these functions can run together on a single system rather than requiring separate instruments for each step.
Product expert note: Tell our team which steps in your current workflow are still manual, and Inkarp will confirm which modules close that gap.
